```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, cache = TRUE)
library(pwr)
library(reticulate)
use_virtualenv("~/.venvs/trial-power")
```

# Design

The trial will randomise whole classes, not individual pupils, to
either the structured phonics intervention or business as usual.
Outcomes are measured on the standardised reading test at the end of
the school year. Because pupils within a class are more alike than
pupils in different classes, the effective sample size is smaller than
the number of pupils.

The design effect for a cluster-randomised trial with $m$ pupils per
class and intraclass correlation $\rho$ is

$$
\text{DE} = 1 + (m - 1)\rho .
$$

With $m =$ `r params$n_per_class` and $\rho =$ `r params$icc`, the
design effect is `r 1 + (params$n_per_class - 1) * params$icc`.

# Assumptions

- Minimum detectable effect: $d = 0.25$, in line with the median effect
  of comparable interventions [@slavin2009].
- Two-sided $\alpha = 0.05$, power $1 - \beta = 0.80$.
- ICC of `r params$icc`, taken from the pilot data and consistent with
  @hedges2007 for reading outcomes in primary schools.
- Attrition of 10% of pupils by follow-up.

# Calculation in R

```{r power-r}
n_indiv <- pwr.t.test(d = 0.25, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.05)$n
de <- 1 + (params$n_per_class - 1) * params$icc
n_per_arm <- ceiling(n_indiv * de / 0.9)
n_classes <- ceiling(n_per_arm / params$n_per_class)
```

Ignoring clustering, we would need `r ceiling(n_indiv)` pupils per arm.
After inflating for the design effect and attrition, we need
`r n_per_arm` pupils per arm, which is `r n_classes` classes per arm.

# Cross-check in Python

A colleague's simulation code, run through reticulate, gives a
similar answer:

```{python sim, eval=TRUE}
import numpy as np
from statsmodels.stats.power import TTestIndPower

icc = r.params["icc"]
m = r.params["n_per_class"]
de = 1 + (m - 1) * icc
n = TTestIndPower().solve_power(effect_size=0.25, power=0.8, alpha=0.05)
print(round(n * de / 0.9))
```

```{python}
# simulation-based check, 2,000 replications
rng = np.random.default_rng(20240115)
```

# Sensitivity

```{r fig-sens, fig.cap="Classes per arm required as a function of the ICC.", echo=FALSE, fig.height=3}
iccs <- seq(0.05, 0.25, by = 0.01)
k <- sapply(iccs, function(r) ceiling(n_indiv * (1 + (params$n_per_class - 1) * r) / 0.9 / params$n_per_class))
plot(iccs, k, type = "s", xlab = "ICC", ylab = "Classes per arm")
```

| ICC  | Design effect | Classes per arm |
|-----:|--------------:|----------------:|
| 0.10 |          3.10 |              36 |
| 0.15 |          4.15 |              48 |
| 0.20 |          5.20 |              60 |

If the ICC turns out higher than 0.15, the trial will be underpowered
for $d = 0.25$. Recruiting 50 classes per arm gives some margin.
